title: CodeChallenge: Math with tokens and embeddings

cues.en: I had a lot of fun creating this code challenge, and I hope you enjoy working through it as well.
cues.zh: 設計這個程式挑戰時，我玩得很開心，希望你做的時候也一樣。

cues.en: We are going to explore whether and how basic arithmetic can be done with tokens and embedding vectors.
cues.zh: 要探索，能否以及如何用 token 與嵌入向量，進行基本算術。

cues.en: Spoiler alert you cannot do real world arithmetic directly with tokens, but along the way to making

cues.en: And then at the end, I will have some discussion about tokens versus embedding vectors.
cues.zh: 最後，也會討論 token 與嵌入向量的差別，

cues.en: And I will say a few things about the implications of what you will discover in this code challenge for actually trying to get Llms to do math correctly.
cues.zh: 並談這個挑戰的發現，對讓 LLM 正確做數學，有什麼意涵。

cues.en: The goal of exercise one is to find the tokens associated with all of these numbers that you see listed here.

cues.zh: 找出並印出每個數字的 token。

cues.en: It's pretty interesting to see that all of these whole numbers are represented by single tokens.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，這些整數都用單一 token 表示。

cues.en: Now once you have this code to produce this output, you can try other numbers.
cues.zh: 有了產生這份輸出的程式，就能試其他數字。

cues.en: You can try dividing these numbers by two to see how that changes the tokenization and so on.
cues.zh: 例如，把數字除以 2，看看斷詞如何改變。

cues.en: The main point is that you cannot do math with tokens because tokens are completely arbitrarily mapped to words and numbers.
cues.zh: 主要重點是，不能直接用 token 做數學，因為 token 與單字、數字的映射完全任意。

cues.en: That is to say, we could completely randomly scramble all of the mappings between token integers and the subwords that they correspond to.

cues.en: Of course, if we did that, we would need to retrain the whole model, but the point is that the mapping cannot be used for mathematical operations.
cues.zh: 當然，這樣就得重新訓練整個模型；但重點是，不能直接用映射編號進行數學運算。

cues.en: On the other hand, the embeddings vectors actually are meaningful, certainly within each embeddings matrix.
cues.zh: 另一方面，嵌入向量確實有意義，至少在同一嵌入矩陣內如此。

cues.en: Now, as you learn from the previous couple of videos, it is tricky to directly compare vectors across different embeddings matrices.

cues.en: But if you're working within the same embeddings matrix, then you really can do math with these vectors, and in some cases you will get meaningful results.

cues.en: Anyway, I want to close this video with one practical tip.
cues.zh: 最後，以一個實用技巧結束。

cues.en: If you want an LLM like ChatGPT to actually solve math problems, especially if the math involves arithmetic
cues.zh: 如果想讓 ChatGPT 這類 LLM 真正解數學題，尤其涉及算術

cues.en: or algebra, it's much better to ask the model to write code to solve the problem, rather than asking the model to solve the problem directly.
cues.zh: 或代數，最好請模型寫程式解題，而不是直接要求它解題。

cues.en: And that is because GPT understands what it means to multiply two large numbers, but it doesn't necessarily have the ability to multiply those numbers by itself.
cues.zh: GPT 理解兩個大數相乘的意義，但不一定有能力，自己完成乘法。

cues.en: So ChatGPT can write code to use as a tool to solve math problems, even if it cannot solve those problems itself.
cues.zh: 所以，即使自己無法解題，ChatGPT 仍能寫程式，把它當成工具來解數學題。

cues.en: And honestly, that's very similar to the level of math abilities of a lot of humans, including me.
cues.zh: 老實說，這和許多人，包括我在內的數學能力，很相似。
